summary: 401 invalid_token failures on auth-service POST /v1/token/validate began sharply at ~14:02 (auth-service error_rate 0.16% at 14:01 -> 36.08% at 14:02; api-gateway 5xx 0.2% -> ~21%; api-gateway first invalid_token log 14:02:22Z). The failure is partial and steady (~36%) and confined to token validation; auth-service resources, latency, restarts and its datastore/cache dependencies are all healthy. Two auth-service changes landed in the 14:00-14:01 minute interval, immediately before onset: deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 upgrading jjwt 0.11->0.12 with a 'breaking parser API' and a rewritten TokenValidator (config_change-adjacent), and config change cfg-2705 rotating jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04. Both remain live (no rollback). The auth-service logs that would show the actual rejection reason are unsearchable (log pipeline down; query_logs 503). Because the two candidate triggers are co-timed within ~60s and the internal error text is unavailable, I cannot mechanically separate a config_change (key rotation, exact historical match HIST-108) from a bad_deployment (JWT library upgrade, HIST-109). Outcome is inconclusive; H1 (config_change) and H2 (bad_deployment) are near-equal, with H1 slightly favored by the exact historical symptom match and the partial-failure/old-token-cohort shape.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) caused 401 invalid_token
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled jwt.signing.key_id rotation at 14:01 (k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) made auth-service reject tokens signed under the previous key id (or pods that had not loaded the new JWKS), producing a steady ~36% invalid_token rate on POST /v1/token/validate from 14:02 onward.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotates signing key id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01
tokens bearing the old kid / pods with stale JWKS fail validation
auth-service returns 401 invalid_token for ~36% of validations from 14:02

assumptions: auth-service validates tokens by resolving the signing key id, and tokens minted before the rotation carry the old kid
the rotation was published without a staged JWKS rollout, as in HIST-108

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.3.0 JWT library upgrade (dep-5710) broke token validation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-5710 at 14:00 upgraded jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 ('breaking parser API') and rewrote TokenValidator, introducing a regression that rejects a subset of otherwise-valid tokens, yielding the steady ~36% invalid_token rate from 14:02.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 rewrites token validation with a breaking jjwt parser API change at 14:00
new validator rejects a subset of tokens

assumptions: the rewritten validator mishandles a token class (e.g. clock skew or key handling) producing partial rather than total failure
no canary limited the failure to a subset of instances

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity/resource or dependency fault at auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service 401s stem from resource exhaustion or a downstream dependency (redis-cache, user-db, kyc-provider) degrading.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU/memory/latency/restarts are flat, redis and user-db show no errors, and kyc-provider is unrelated to token validation; the onset is a clean step coincident with two auth-service changes, not a load ramp.

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate jumped from 0.16% (14:01) to 36.08% (14:02) and stayed ~34-38%.
api-gateway logged 401 invalid_token for POST /v1/token/validate starting 14:02:22Z; it is the only warning pattern.
auth-service deploy dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00 is live, not rolled back.
auth-service config cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01.
api-gateway 5xx rose to ~21% in the 14:00 bucket and held steady.
auth-service CPU, memory, latency, request_rate, rate-limit and restarts stayed flat; redis/user-db healthy.
auth-service logs are unsearchable (query_logs 503 on all attempts).
HIST-108 is an exact historical match for key-rotation-induced 401s; HIST-109 matches a library-upgrade regression.
The failure is partial and steady (~36%), not a step to ~100%.

assumptions: auth-service validates tokens by resolving the token's signing key id against a JWKS/store, so a rotation can invalidate tokens carrying the old kid
the observed 401 invalid_token is generated by auth-service's validation logic (not an upstream proxy)
the auth-service version running before 14:00 had no equivalent failure (no earlier 401s observed)
the 14:00 deploy and 14:01 rotation are independent changes (not part of one coordinated release)

timeline.event: auth-service error_rate normal ~0.2%; no invalid_token logs at api-gateway.
auth-service deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) goes live.
auth-service error_rate jumps to 36.08%; api-gateway 5xx jumps to ~7-21%.
First api-gateway '401 invalid_token' log for POST /v1/token/validate.
Incident INC-007 reported (SEV-1); auth-service logs unsearchable.
466 invalid_token warnings logged; failure rate still steady ~21% at gateway, no rollback performed.

recommended_actions.action: Restore/repair the identity-namespace log pipeline and re-query auth-service logs for the exact token-validation rejection reason (kid mismatch vs parser error).
recommended_actions.rationale: The decisive evidence separating a key-rotation event from a JWT-parser regression is the internal rejection message, which is currently unsearchable (F7).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or revert the JWT signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (re-publish previous key id k-2025-10 / staged JWKS rollout) as the first mitigation, since it is the exact-match historical pattern.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-108 resolution was exactly 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation'; a single config revert is low-risk.

recommended_actions.action: If key-rotation revert does not restore validation, roll back auth-service deploy dep-5710 to the previous version to test the parser-regression hypothesis.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5710 is a breaking jjwt parser upgrade that is still live; a rollback cleanly tests H2.

recommended_actions.action: Add staged/canary JWKS rollout and negative-validation smoke tests for token validation on future key rotations and JWT library upgrades.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both candidate causes are change-management failures that a staged rollout plus validation smoke test would catch.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unsearchable (query_logs 503) — the actual token-validation rejection reason (kid mismatch, signature error, parse exception) is unknown, which is the key discriminator between H1 and H2.
No pod-level / per-instance view of auth-service to check whether failure is limited to a subset of instances (would favor a partial rollout or stale-JWKS pod).
No token-level detail (issuer kid, issuance time) to confirm whether failures correlate with tokens minted before 14:01 (rotation) vs. a token class (parser).
No rollback has been performed for either change, so recovery-on-rollback cannot be used to confirm causality.

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate (unit '% of requests') was flat ~0.2% through 14:01 and jumped to 36.08% at the 14:02 minute bucket, staying ~34-38% thereafter.
api-gateway began logging 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token' at 14:02:22Z; 466 such WARN entries by 15:58 and this is the ONLY warning pattern present.

findings.statement: auth-service deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation' with changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten' was deployed at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z and is still live (never rolled back).
auth-service config change cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id old k-2025-10 -> new k-2026-04, 'Scheduled signing-key rotation' by security-automation) occurred at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z.
api-gateway 5xx error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~21% in the 14:00 bucket and held steady at ~21% through 15:52.

auth-service CPU (~38%), memory (~52%), latency_p99 (~90ms), request_rate (~400 rps), rate_limited (~2/min) and restarts (0) all stayed flat across the incident; redis-cache and user-db logs show no error patterns.
auth-service logs could not be retrieved: query_logs returned 'backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)' on every attempt (three separate calls).

Historical incident HIST-108 (2025-10-01) is an exact symptom match: '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change.
